name: LeKiwi (stock)
description: LeKiwi mobile base (3 omni wheels) + SO-101 arm, exactly as the upstream repo ships it.

source.files: urdf/LeKiwi.urdf, meshes/ (URDF/meshes), print/ (3DPrintMeshes) - copied verbatim, see SOURCE.md

frame.notes: robot frame, mm: +X right, +Y forward, +Z up; top deck plate Z = 57.0, shoulder-pan axis at (0, 67.15)

kinematics.scale_note: URDF lengths are metres, the referenced meshes are millimetres and carry no <mesh scale>; multiply link poses by 1000 after FK (or the meshes by 0.001 before).
kinematics.joint_limits_source: Source: TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100, Simulation/SO101/so101_new_calib.urdf (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100/main/Simulation/SO101/so101_new_calib.urdf, fetched 2026-09-12) -- the only SO-101 description that carries <limit> tags. Its <limit> values, in degrees: shoulder_pan +-110, shoulder_lift +-100, elbow_flex +-96.83, wrist_flex +-95, wrist_roll -157.21..+162.79, gripper -10..+100. The LeKiwi URDF (external/LeKiwi/URDF/LeKiwi.urdf) has NO <limit> tags and, more importantly, a DIFFERENT joint zero: its zero pose is the folded/parked CAD configuration (upper arm horizontal backwards, forearm folded forward again) while the reference zero has the upper arm up and the forearm forward. The mapping q_lekiwi = sign * q_ref + offset_deg was solved geometrically, not guessed: both URDFs describe the same physical arm, so for each joint the axis LINE (point + direction) of every downstream joint must coincide once the two chains are aligned by one rigid transform. Fitting sign+offset per joint over 6-8 random configurations leaves max axis-line offset 5.1 mm and max axis-angle 0.87 deg (identity mapping: 254 mm / 180 deg; the best wrong sign combination: 145x worse cost), the residual being the genuine CAD difference between the two exports (forearm 136.0 vs 135.0 mm, two DH offsets 1.5 and 3.5 mm apart). Signs: pan +1, lift/elbow/wrist_flex/wrist_roll/gripper -1 -- i.e. every LeKiwi arm axis except the shoulder pan points the opposite way to the SO-101 reference axis. The pan offset is not observable from geometry (a base rotation absorbs it) and is taken as 0, which is correct by inspection: at pan 0 the arm points robot +Y in both models, and the limit is symmetric anyway. The gripper offset is likewise not observable from the axis lines (nothing is downstream of it), and a mesh test cannot find it either: the stock jaw pivots INSIDE its own bracket, so Moving_Jaw_08d-v1 intersects Wrist_Roll_08c-v1 at every angle from -120 to +103 deg in the decimated meshes. It is taken as 0 on the finger-tip measurement instead: tip separation (moving-jaw tip to fixed-finger tip, collide.js gripOpening) falls monotonically 142.2 mm at -100, 62.7 at -30, 41.6 at -15, 20.1 at 0, 7.1 at +10, with its minimum 6.2 mm at +15 -- so LeKiwi arm_gripper 0 is the near-closed jaw exactly as the reference's 0 is, +10 is the closed stop (matching the reference's 10 deg of over-close) and NEGATIVE arm_gripper OPENS. This also agrees with the app's own presets, which use arm_gripper -30 for the two reaching poses. SANITY: the LeKiwi URDF zero pose (all six joints 0) lands inside every one of these ranges, 3.8..69.3 deg from the nearest stop -- as a parked CAD pose should. CAVEAT for the app: three of the four presets shipped in v3 were authored before any limit existed and fall OUTSIDE this range -- stowed (lift +40, wrist_flex -54), reach floor (lift +20, elbow -76), reach table (lift +9). Only 'raised max' is legal. Independently of the limits, collide.js finds those same three presets to be in HARD COLLISION with the robot (upper arm through Base_08q / the WaveShare plate / the deck plate), so they are not merely out of travel, they are impossible. See the SO-101 motion reference for IK-corrected replacements that hit the same tip positions. arm_joint_range_deg above is the OLD UI travel hint and is kept only so that nothing that reads it breaks; joint_limits_deg is the physical one.
kinematics.zero_pose_note: The URDF zero pose is the folded/parked CAD configuration, NOT the SO-101 reference zero; joint_limits_map carries the sign+offset that relates the two. All six joints at 0 is inside every limit.

deck_grid.note: top deck plate bolt grid: 20 mm pitch, Z 57, usable radius 107, hole Ø3.50 (M3 clearance), measured on the deck mesh

wrist_flange.axes: +X = the arm_wrist_roll axis (finger direction), +Z = -arm_gripper hinge axis, +Y = Z x X
wrist_flange.note: PincOpen assembly frame -> robot frame at the arm ZERO pose. APPROXIMATE, derived from the stock gripper. +X = the arm_wrist_roll axis (0,0.42262,-0.90631), the stock finger direction. +Z = -arm_gripper hinge axis (0,0.90631,0.42262), so the PincOpen camera stack points the same way as the stock wrist camera bracket. +Y = Z x X = robot -X, the stock jaw opening direction. Origin: the PincOpen back face (full-gripper X_min = -53.49 mm) is put on the wrist-roll output flange; the stock fixed jaw starts 1.0 mm behind it. The PincOpen mirror plane Y=0 and finger mid-plane Z=0 are put on the stock gripper centreline. Assumed: PincOpen bolts straight onto the wrist-roll flange with no adapter plate; no CAD of the real adapter was available. Expect a few mm of error along +X.

cameras.label: Front
cameras.name: Front (navigation)
cameras.note: DEVICE ONLY - this entry is the camera, not a mount. The fitted front camera option publishes the pose: the stock bracket carries the URDF datum, and removing it switches the camera off.
cameras.pose_derivation: camera <- Camera-Model-v3 link frame (mm), column-major: col0 = image right, col1 = image up, col2 = -optical axis, col3 = sensor point. Derived from the URDF visual origin of the link (xyz -0.01601 0.00243 -0.01139, rpy 1.74533 1.39626 -pi) plus meshes/Camera-Model-v3.stl: a 38 × 38 × 3 mm board at mesh z 0..3 with an M12 lens barrel (r 6.1..6.8) from z 3 to 21.5, so the optical axis is mesh +Z and the sensor is the board front face, mesh (0,0,3). At the base pose that is robot (0, 111.75, 25.05) aiming (0, 0.98481, 0.17365) = +Y, 10.000° ABOVE horizontal (verified: the axis ray clears Camera-Mount-v8 and every stock mesh, never meets the ground, and matches a photograph of the real front feed). robot_matrix is the same pose already multiplied through FK, used when ctx.fk cannot resolve the link.

source.derivation: All three cameras on the robot are the JR DF200 "100° without distortion" module, streamed MJPG at 640 × 480 (user-confirmed 2026-09-15). 100° on the DIAGONAL of a rectilinear 4:3 frame is 2*atan(tan(50)*4/5) = 87.3° horizontal, 2*atan(tan(50)*3/5) = 71.1° vertical. This is a hardware fact, not a fit: the fitted numbers this package shipped before are the alternatives beside it.

alternatives.label: measured from the top feed
alternatives.note: A two-landmark (front omni-wheel tops) fit of one screenshot of the live top feed. It is under-determined - tilt and FOV trade against each other - and at the confirmed 87.3 the same screenshot no longer reproduces: its wheel spacing and its silhouette scale want 60-66. The screenshot is most likely a crop. Kept so the old coverage numbers can be reproduced.
alternatives.url: measured: fit of the live top-camera feed, 2026-09-12

alternatives.label: measured from the wrist feed
alternatives.note: A three-landmark (servo LED, gripper body top edge, fingertip) least-squares fit of the real wrist feed: 32.7° half-vFOV, i.e. 65.4° V = 81° H at 4:3. The three landmarks solved separately give 74.6 / 83.3 / 90.8, mean 82.9 - the confirmed 87.3 is inside that spread.
alternatives.url: measured: least-squares fit of the real wrist image, 2026-09-13

alternatives.label: Arducam OV5648 (LeKiwi BOM)
alternatives.note: The camera the upstream LeKiwi BOM lists for base_camera_mount.stl: Arducam 5MP OV5648 wide-angle USB, "Field of View (FOV): 90 degree (H)", M12 lens. It is the camera the URDF models; it is not the one on this robot.

alternatives.label: 110° diagonal wide-angle
alternatives.note: Arducam B0454, "5MP OV5648, 110 Degree DFOV Wide Angle". 110° on the diagonal of a rectilinear 4:3 frame is 97.6° H / 81.2° V.

alternatives.label: conservative 90° diagonal (2026-08)
alternatives.note: The 2026-08 coverage sweep assumed a 90° diagonal lens as ±33° horizontal and ±25° vertical, i.e. 66° H. That is conservative: a rectilinear 90° diagonal at 4:3 is 77.3° H. Kept so the old coverage numbers can be reproduced.

gripper.label: Gripper
gripper.hint: What is bolted to the wrist-roll flange.
gripper.note: This package attaches nothing, so it offers no PincOpen option - swapping in a whole gripper package is what the LeKiwi + PincOpen package is for.

options.label: Stock SO-101 jaw
options.note: The single-jaw gripper in the URDF, driven by arm_gripper: the fixed jaw it closes onto, the moving jaw and the servo that drives it.

front_camera.label: Front camera
front_camera.hint: The forward-looking camera on the base bracket.

front.source: the stock LeKiwi front bracket, recovered from the URDF visual origin of Camera-Model-v3 (see the package note). `tilt_deg` is nose-down in the CARRIER frame (this camera link); in the ROBOT frame, at the URDF zero pose, the lens sits -10° nose-down. Intrinsics from user-confirmed hardware: JR DF200, 2026-09-15.

wrist_camera_mount.label: Wrist camera mount
wrist_camera_mount.hint: The camera that looks down the fingers.

wrist.source: the stock SO-101 wrist bracket (Wrist-Camera-Mount-v11), recovered from the URDF: the camera-in-mesh transform of the front module Camera-Model-v3, re-applied to the Camera-Model-v3-1 instance the wrist carries - the two are the same mesh. `tilt_deg` is nose-down in the CARRIER frame (this camera link); in the ROBOT frame, at the URDF zero pose, the lens sits 80° nose-down. Intrinsics from user-confirmed hardware: JR DF200, 2026-09-15.

pi_case.label: Raspberry Pi case
pi_case.hint: The Pi enclosure on the rear deck.

presets.label: Stowed
presets.note: Parked, folded over the deck - the URDF zero pose. Legal on every joint and clear of the robot.

presets.label: Reach floor
presets.note: Gripper down at the floor, tip at about (-6.6, 322.9, -5.8) mm.

presets.label: Reach table
presets.note: Tip at about (-4.8, 237.9, 242.8) mm, roughly a 240 mm table top.

presets.label: Raised max
presets.note: Arm raised, tip at about (-4.8, 154.6, 566.2) mm.

presets_source: Four arm poses, corrected against the joint limits. The set this studio shipped earlier was authored before any limit existed: three of those four broke a limit and were in hard collision with the robot, so these replacements hit the same tip positions from inside the limits. One example: Reach floor holds arm_wrist_flex at 170.5, not the 171 the earlier table printed, because 171 is 0.5° past the -19.5..170.5 stop. Angles are degrees in the LeKiwi URDF convention; kinematics.joint_limits_map relates them to the SO-101 reference zero.

mass.source: Upstream publishes no weight. Seeed Studio LeKiwi Kit 12 V (base, printed parts, battery, no Pi, no cameras, no arm) is listed at 1.7 kg. Add the Raspberry Pi 5 with its cooler (0.06 kg), two USB cameras (0.02 kg), the six arm STS3215 servos at 55 g each (Feetech, 0.33 kg) and the printed SO-101 arm parts by the sim's volume rule (0.34 kg). The band is that 2.45 kg ±15 %.
